subject: Post-demo model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jane Li <jane.li@acme.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 10, 2026 at 4:22 PM
Subject: Post-demo model shortlist & next steps

Hi Jane / Tom 

Thanks again for your time today - great conversation and really helpful context on the user flows you want to protect for Acme (customer support triage + automated reply drafts + executive summarization). Quick recap and a recommended model shortlist based on the tradeoffs we discussed (cost / latency / quality).

Recap from demo:
- Primary workload: conversational reply generation at ~512 token prompts, 1-3k user requests/day initially.
- SLO targets: p95 latency < 800ms for short replies, p50 < 250ms for typical prompts.
- Key quality concerns: minimal hallucination for factual recall, conservative tone for customer-facing replies.

Recommended shortlist (high-level rationale):
1) Redwood-8B-quant (recommended) - Best fit if you prioritize latency/cost. Lower memory footprint (good for Dedicated), strong instruction-following after our calibration prompts. Tradeoff: slightly lower factuality on long-context queries.
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (balanced) - Good middle ground: solid quality with reasonable latency and predictable costs. Strong on instruction-following out of the box.
3) LlamaX-33B (high-quality) - Highest quality for edge cases and complex summarization, but higher token cost and p95 latency; consider only for routes that require highest accuracy.

Attachments: I've attached a short PDF with side-by-side cost/latency/quality notes and our proposed prompt sets (acme_model_shortlist.pdf, prompt_set_examples.md). We'll also send a small benchmark export after we run the two-model eval.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood runs a short evaluation (2-3 days) using your canonical prompt set against Redwood-8B-quant and Mistral-Instruct-7B. We'll provide a shared eval dashboard and the raw outputs for review.
- We'll include an A/B run for the top route (support replies) and produce quality metrics (ROUGE/F1 where applicable + human spot checks for hallucinations).
- Schedule: Can we target next-week window for the eval? Please confirm preferred days and any procurement/legal contacts we should loop in.

Relevant links:
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/ACME-2026-RED-01
- Benchmarks (incoming): https://drive.google.com/acme/model-benchmarks

Thanks - happy to jump on a 15-min sync if you'd like to walk the shortlist.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Jane Li <jane.li@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 9:05 AM
Subject: Re: Post-demo model shortlist & next steps

Thanks Marissa
this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we lock the eval window:

- Can you provide expected cost per 1M input+output tokens for each model (ballpark is fine)?
- For Redwood-8B-quant and Mistral-Instruct-7B, what are p50/p95 latencies we should expect at 512-token prompts on dedicated capacity vs hosted?
- Hallucination risk: do you have any existing evals or observed failure modes for knowledge-heavy prompts?

Procurement: looping in procurement@acme.com (bcc)
they will need a rough SOW and cost estimate.

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood will run human spot checks, or we should supply reviewers? We can provide 50 labeled examples if helpful.

Cheers,
Jane
Head of Product
Acme Corp

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jane Li <jane.li@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 11:18 AM
Subject: Re: Post-demo model shortlist & next steps

Hi Jane
Vivek from Solutions (looping in Priyom). Quick answers + a short benchmark snapshot attached.

Ballpark cost (hosted API, current list rates)
input+output combined, approximate:
- Redwood-8B-quant: ~$15 per 1M tokens
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: ~$28 per 1M tokens
- LlamaX-33B: ~$140 per 1M tokens

Latency (observed on Dedicated GPU pools, 512-token prompt + 128-token generation):
- Redwood-8B-quant: p50 ~140ms, p95 ~420ms
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: p50 ~220ms, p95 ~560ms
- LlamaX-33B: p50 ~420ms, p95 ~1.1s

Notes on hallucinations / quality:
- Redwood-8B-quant: after targeted calibration prompts and a small prompt-template adjustment, factuality for short customer-reply templates is acceptable; it struggles on multi-hop recall (long documents). We recommend using the KV cache + prefix/context retrieval pattern for any long-context facts.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: fewer outright hallucinations on short QA-style prompts; stronger instruction adherence.
- LlamaX-33B: best across the board but cost/latency tradeoff limits it to selective routes.

Attached: acme_benchmarks_20260310.xlsx
contains p50/p95 distributions from a 1k-sample synthetic workload and the evaluation prompts we used. We'll run the same harness with your real prompt set during the eval.

We can run human spot checks: Redwood provides a small human review pool for evaluation (up to 100 samples) or we can accept your labeled 50 examples. Either works. For the A/B, we usually surface: BLEU/ROUGE (where applicable), semantic similarity, and a human hallucination flag.

If Acme is concerned about p95 latency, we can configure a routing rule: route 95th-percentile-sensitive requests to Mistral-Instruct-7B/Dedicated with higher SLA and route bulk traffic to Redwood-8B-quant for cost savings.


Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: acme_benchmarks_20260310.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks Vivek
and thanks Jane. Quick synthesis and proposed plan:

1) Eval scope (recommended):
   - Models: Redwood-8B-quant (cost-optimized) vs Mistral-Instruct-7B (balanced).
   - Eval duration: 48-372 hours using your canonical prompt set (you can send 50-200 examples).
   - Outputs: shared Drive folder with raw outputs + a short dashboard (accuracy metrics + hallucination flags) + the benchmark sheet (attached).

2) Procurement / SOW:
   - We'll provide a short SOW and cost estimate for the eval (no charge for the 48-372 hour eval itself). Post-eval pricing options will include Hosted API rates and a Dedicated Reserved capacity proposal if you want to lock in lower unit costs.
   - DocuSign SOW link (placeholder): https://app.redwood.com/sow/ACME-2026-RED-01

3) Human review: Redwood can run up to 100 spot-check reviews; if you supply 50 labeled examples we will incorporate them into the eval dashboard.

Please confirm: would next Wed (Mar 18) or Thu (Mar 19) work for the eval window? Also confirm the procurement contact so we can send the SOW to the right person.

Attachments: acme_model_shortlist.pdf, prompt_set_examples.md, acme_benchmarks_20260310.xlsx


Marissa
